title: Nutrition through the life cycle
kicker: Lesson 10 of your course. Test practice uses checked answers, because there is no official key for this test.
html:
This lesson covers nutrition at each life stage: infancy, childhood, adolescence, adult men and women, pregnancy, breastfeeding, menopause and older age.

Key idea: The lesson notes for Lesson 10 are not in the study hub yet, so this lesson has test practice only.

quiz.q: Which of the following would NOT be considered a benefit of breastfeeding?
o: Breast milk provides the right nourishment and has more available iron, vitamins A and C, niacin, potassium and the right amino acids for growth than any natural or formulated substitute
Breastfeeding stimulates uterine contractions, reducing bleeding and bringing the uterus back to its normal size

Breast milk has lactase, which is the enzyme for digesting lactose, so the baby gets both the milk sugar (lactose) and the enzyme needed to digest it. This is important because the baby’s liver cannot make lactase during the first months of life.
Breast milk filters out pesticides so the baby is protected from contaminants
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key.

Likes and dislikes can often limit the diets of 5 to 13 year olds
Many parent overestimate their children’s needs and the amount of food required
Offering a sweet as a reward for eating vegetables is helpful with a picky eater
During the middle years, the average youngster gains between 5 and 8 lbs and grows about half an inch per year provided they have the nutrients they need.

quiz.q: During adolescence, what is the rate of growth for boys and girls?
o: Young men may gain 15 to 20 lbs and grow 4 to 5 inches in height per year, while girls may gain 13 to 18 lbs and grow 3 to 4 inches per year
Young men may gain 10 to15 lbs and grow 4 to 5 inches in height per year, while girls may gain 13 to 18 lbs and grow 3 to 4 inches per year
Young men may gain 15 to 20 lbs and grow 2 to 4 inches in height per year, while girls may gain 13 to 18 lbs and grow 3 to 4 inches per year
Young men may gain 15 to 20 lbs and grow 4 to 5 inches in height per year, while girls may gain 10 to 15 lbs and grow 3 to 4 inches per year

quiz.q: Which of the following statements regarding adult women and nutrition is FALSE?
o: Women put on weight easily and have a difficult time losing it; even low calorie diets may not do the trick. Changing food quality may help more than calorie counting
Calcium, magnesium, and niacin may be helpful for menstrual cramps
During menopause, bioidentical hormones may be tolerated better and carry fewer risks than synthetic hormones
Women tend to do best on a moderate calorie diet that includes a good amount of protein and vegetables, some whole grains, as well as nuts, seeds, and a good amount of fruits

o: Nutritional requirements are much the same as during pregnancy, with even higher requirements for many nutrients and reduced needs for a few

quiz.q: Menopause represents a major transition in the lives of most women. Which of the following recommendations for menopause would be considered FALSE?
o: During menopause, it is wise for women to get adequate sleep and even take naps if they feel tired because it can also be a time of lowered energy
A good diet along with supportive nutritional supplements and stress management may help to delay the onset of menopause and reduce the symptoms when they occur
Premenopausal women should regularly consume at least 1,200 to 1,500 mg of calcium per day. Squeezing lemon juice or adding apple cider vinegar to leafy greens helps to maximize calcium absorption
Vitamin D and E can often help with hot flashes and night sweats, as can cohosh and licorice root
L-tryptophan should be avoided as it can exacerbate fatigue
